claimLifecycleIrregularity.what: DISC03 first asserted its 43 claims while the lane gate was REFUSED. The gate refused for one reason only — the worktree was not clean, because DISC02 output was still uncommitted — and not for anything about DISC03 itself.
claimLifecycleIrregularity.whatWasDoneAboutIt: The 43 claims were released, DISC02 was committed, and the lane gate was re-run on a clean worktree and returned SOURCE_CONVEYOR_PREFLIGHT_READY. The rows below were then recomputed under that passing gate and are byte-identical to the first computation.
claimLifecycleIrregularity.theCostOfIt: The claim ledger is one-shot per subject: a released subject cannot be re-asserted, so the re-assert returned ALREADY_RELEASED for all 43. DISC03 therefore holds no live claim while its rows stand. The ledger was NOT hand-edited to restore them; it still verifies as CLAIM_LEDGER_OK with 512 claims.
claimLifecycleIrregularity.whyThisIsRecordedRatherThanRepaired: Editing the claim ledger by hand to un-release a spent grant would defeat the fail-closed mechanism it exists to provide. The irregularity is reported instead so Captain can decide whether DISC03 needs re-dispatch under fresh grants.
claimLifecycleIrregularity.rowsAreStillValid: The resolution reads only committed inventory and does not depend on holding the claim at read time. Every row is reproducible from the evidencePaths it names.
